about: Stolen SNAP benefits: what to do, with Florida's steps.

rows.plain: The federal program that replaced stolen SNAP benefits ended on December 20, 2024. Replacing stolen benefits is no longer guaranteed.
In Florida, file a police report with your local law enforcement agency and ask for a replacement EBT card. Call EBT Customer Service at 1-888-356-3281, or use your MyACCESS account.
Florida offers ebtEDGE (website or app): you can freeze your card so no transactions go through, and block out-of-state and online transactions. Unfreeze it when you shop.
In other states, contact your local SNAP office if your benefits were stolen, and change your PIN right away. USDA lists each state's EBT customer service number.
State agencies and EBT processors never call or text to ask for your card number or PIN. Anyone who does is a scammer.
Change your PIN often, right before your benefits are added each month.
